provenance.why: First genuine named encounter in the Hub — needs a stable identity so she can recur and the Steadwood passage can be a t

offscreen.note: Siol remained at the Hub plaza through the cooler part of the morning, watching the foot-traffic shift, neither departing nor inquiring — present in the way that costs nothing yet, and costs something.

Someone at the plaza asked Siol directly where they were going and why, in a tone that made 'nowhere in particular' sound like an accusation — the world pressed in, and for a moment the going-on felt less possible than it had the day before.

A plaza vendor who had grown used to Siol's quiet presence reported them to a Hub registrar as a loiterer without a declared purpose, and now there is a notice requiring Siol to either state their business in writing or move on by the following morning.

A hub official stopped Siol at the plaza's inner gate to check travel papers — the papers are in order, but the stop itself drew looks, and the brief public scrutiny is exactly the kind of attention Siol's quiet passage depends on not receiving.

Someone at the plaza asked them, not unkindly, where they were headed — and Siol gave an answer that was true enough, but the question sat wrong afterward, because going on as they are requires not being asked to name it.

Someone at the plaza recognized Siol from somewhere earlier in their travels and said so aloud, in company — not with malice, but the name now sits in the air among strangers, and Siol cannot take it back.

Siol remained at the plaza's edge another five days, the world continuing its small insistences around them, and they continued to absorb those insistences without quite yielding to any of them — neither pushed out nor pulled in, still just beginning.
Siol kept to their usual circuit of the plaza and spoke to no one new — the world pressed no harder than usual, and they neither yielded nor advanced.

siol-elven-traveler-at-the-hub-plaza-tal.description: Siol — Elven traveler at the Hub plaza, tall, pale coat, bir

maren-voss.name: Maren Voss
maren-voss.role: Liminal fighter who crosses thresholds to win — patient at every gate, lethal the moment one opens
maren-voss.voiceHints: Speaks the way someone waits — fully, without fidgeting. Grey coat, collar up against the early-spring cold she doesn't seem to feel. Answers questions a beat after you expect, not because she's slow but because she's already past your question and choosing which part of the answer is worth giving. Never names her companions first; lets them step through on their own terms.
knowledge: The Waygate's threshold-logic — which passages open early, which resist, and what the valley asks before it lets you through
How to read a bout before it starts: the other fighter's weight on their threshold moment, when they commit, the half-step that gives everything away
That the Coliseum far arc rewards those who make their opponent cross into unfavourable ground — and she has walked every arc of it in her mind

companions.name: Aldric
companions.role: First second — manages her between bouts, reads the crowd for information she won't bother with
companions.note: Older, steady, doesn't smile much; has been at this long enough that his calm is the real kind

companions.name: Pell
companions.role: Second second — young enough to be nervous, sharp enough to be useful; scouts ground and brings her water without being asked
companions.note: Talks when Aldric doesn't, which means the two of them together cover everything

abilities.name: Threshold Step
abilities.description: Maren reads the liminal beat of any exchange — the half-moment a gate swings — and steps through it before her opponent has committed. She does not dodge; she is simply no longer where the blow was aimed, and she is already at the next threshold.

abilities.name: Gate Hold
abilities.description: She can stall a passage — freeze the moment of transition for herself or a companion — holding a threshold open or shut long enough to change the shape of a fight. Used defensively, it is a ward; used offensively, it pins an opponent mid-step.

abilities.name: Far Arc Patience
abilities.description: In the Coliseum's far arc, where sight lines are long and the crowd loses track, Maren goes still enough to become part of the threshold itself — then crosses the distance in a single passage-movement that reads as arrival, not approach.

maren-voss.wants: One clean bout at the far arc, properly offered. She has been at the Waygate since the first thaw, waiting for her name to come up through the right mouth. She does not want shortcuts; she wants the gate to open the right way.
maren-voss.fears: That she will be read as ordinary before the bout begins — that whoever faces her will arrive with a fixed idea of what a grey-coat threshold-walker does, and she will have to spend the whole fight correcting it instead of fighting.

reactsToReputation.patient: a small, real nod — she recognises her own quality in someone else
reactsToReputation.reckless: watches them the way you watch an open gate in a high wind: not afraid, not dismissive, just careful
reactsToReputation.Silas: she has heard the name from Orvil this morning; she has not said anything about it yet, but Aldric noticed she stood up straighter

provenance.hint: a threshold-walker in a grey coat — young, patient, waiting for a bout at the Coliseum far arc, with two companions as s
provenance.why: Orvil named them as Silas's potential opponent this morning — they need a stable identity and craft before the bout can

tane-solr.name: Tane Solr
tane-solr.role: Threshold-walker and named bout opponent — a man who has crossed the center-line enough times to stop counting and started watching the sand instead
tane-solr.voiceHints: Unhurried in a way that is not laziness but arithmetic — he has already run the numbers on you and does not need to rush. Speaks in short declaratives with long pauses between them, as if he is giving the words time to land before he adds more weight. Calls the sand 'the floor' the way carpenters call wood 'the material.' Does not brag. Does not diminish. Names things exactly. When he says your name he means it.
tane-solr.appearance: Lean in the way the valley's early-spring wind is lean — nothing wasted, everything purposeful. Grey coat, collarless, worn to the colour of old flint at the cuffs. Two seconds coiled at his left hip, their grip-wraps re-done so many times the cord beneath has fused into something that is no longer rope and not yet bone. Dawn finds him standing at the far arc before the torches are lit, not warming up, just watching the center-line as if it owes him a conversation.
knowledge: The Waygate Coliseum's far arc — every degree of angle the pre-dawn light hits the sand, and what it does to a fighter's depth perception
How the valley's threshold law reads a bout: where the line is, what crossing it costs, and the three ways experienced fighters use the cost as a weapon
The particular grammar of two seconds — reach, wrap, redirect, the half-breath of slack that telegraphs everything if you know to listen for it
Silas's name, and therefore something about Silas — enough to have agreed to the bout, not enough to have made up his mind
tane-solr.wants: A bout that is true — not won or lost but honest, where both fighters come to the center-line having brought everything they actually are and no more.
tane-solr.fears: That he has crossed so many thresholds he no longer feels them, and that the day he stops feeling the line underfoot is the day he becomes dangerous for the wrong reasons.
tane-solr.history: Tane came up through the valley circuit in a leaner season, when the Coliseum ran bouts by firelight because they could not afford dawn slots. He lost his first twelve named matches and won the thirteenth by not moving when every instinct in the crowd — and his opponent — was certain he would. He has been studying stillness as a weapon ever since. The grey coat was his instructor's; she died between seasons, not on the sand, and he has not replaced it. He is not sentimental about this. He is precise about it.

reactsToReputation.experienced: a single nod — peer-recognition, no ceremony
reactsToReputation.reckless: watches more carefully, says less, waits for the recklessness to teach the lesson he will not deliver in words
reactsToReputation.seeking: will speak plainly, once, about what the center-line actually is — then stops, because the rest has to be walked
reactsToReputation.named_opponent: meets their eyes at the far arc before dawn and lets the sand do the introduction

provenance.hint: Tane Solr — a lean threshold-walker in a grey coat, unhurried, experienced on the sand, waiting with two seconds at the
provenance.why: He is now Silas's named bout opponent at the center-line and will need a stable identity, personality, and history for t

offscreen.note: Tane spent the early part of the day watching two apprentices spar and said nothing, but afterward he smoothed the sand at the center-line himself, a thing he normally leaves to the groundskeepers.
The opponent arranged for today fell through before they reached the floor, and Tane spent the morning hitting the post alone, which told him nothing he didn't already know about himself.
Tane found no partner willing to meet him at the center-line today — every offer that came was laced with something else, pride or performance, and he turned them all down quietly.

The bouts available to Tane in these five days were the usual kind — winnable, manageable, already mapped before the first step — and he showed up for none of them, which is its own kind of answer he isn't ready to look at yet.
Tane sparred twice but both bouts were ordinary — partners who held back, and so did she, and the honest center-line stayed out of reach.

cassiel-ord.name: Cassiel Ord
cassiel-ord.role: Former march-warden who walked away from the post and sat down in the bowl and has not decided what comes next
cassiel-ord.voiceHints: Economy of words born from years of writing terse post-reports nobody acted on. Does not explain himself unless pushed, and when pushed gives one careful sentence more than expected and then stops. The silence after he speaks is not unfriendly — it is the silence of someone who has learned that most follow-up questions answer themselves if you wait. Stillwater grain: surface calm, something held under it that has not been named yet.
knowledge: The March in the years bracketing Veth's posting — patrol routes, seasonal flood-lines, which threshold markers are still true and which have drifted
Why the Veth post was dissolved, or at least the version of it he was given, and the part of it he does not believe
The Raven's Home threshold: he has crossed it twice, knows what it costs, knows what it gives back, and will not say more than that without trust he has not granted yet
Early-spring snowmelt read from limestone and sky — when a valley like this will sheet-flood and how much warning you actually get
The name of whoever ordered the dissolution and what that person's interests are in the March going unwatched
cassiel-ord.wants: To sit here long enough to know whether what he is feeling is conscience or exhaustion — and to answer that honestly before he moves again.
cassiel-ord.fears: That the dissolution was not incompetence but intent, and that knowing it changes what he is obligated to do with the rest of his life.

reactsToReputation.warden_or_posted: goes very still, then asks one quiet question about where and when before he decides anything
reactsToReputation.connected_to_veth: trusts nothing, offers nothing, watches everything — but does not leave
reactsToReputation.civilian_or_outsider: slightly more open; the professional wariness does not apply and he is tired of it anyway
reactsToReputation.trustworthy_established: speaks in longer sentences, eventually stops editing himself

cassiel-ord.appearance: A lean man somewhere in his middle forties, the kind of lean that is not hunger but habit — he has been moving through difficult ground for a long time and his body organized itself around that. March-warden coat, wool, the grey-green of limestone shadow, one brass closure replaced with knotted cord. Boots still muddy from the threshold. He is sitting with his back to the outcrop and his knees drawn up, not sleeping — just not moving. His face is weather-seamed and unhurried, the expression of someone who has decided to be still until he is ready not to be. There is a short-handled field axe laid flat beside him, not gripped, not put away.
cassiel-ord.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Kind and domain are independent: a people tends toward positions, an individual holds their own.
cassiel-ord.functionsNote: Reveal: carries March knowledge the players cannot otherwise access cleanly. Bind: his loyalty to the post's dissolution-secret creates a tension that hooks the scene forward. Conceal: he is actively withholding the threshold-crossing account until trust is established — the concealment is the scene's pressure valve.
cassiel-ord.inGrainNote: Stillwater's Trouble grain: peace + falsehood — the bowl is quiet and the quiet is not honest. Cassiel sits in both registers: genuinely still, genuinely not ready to tell the truth. Early-spring sets the mood — snowmelt, limestone cold, the world pretending winter is done.

provenance.hint: A figure sitting against the limestone outcrop at the far edge of Stillwater's Trouble — someone who walked here from th
provenance.why: The boot-tracks that ended at the Raven's Home threshold belong to someone, and that someone is sitting in the bowl righ

offscreen.note: Cassiel sat with it another night and still could not say which one it was — the feeling has not clarified, only persisted, and he hasn't moved.

After five days of sitting with it, Cassiel has narrowed the question at least this far: the feeling sharpens in the mornings and dulls toward evening, which is the rhythm of conscience, not exhaustion — he hasn't answered it yet, but he knows now what he is actually asking.
Cassiel sat through a second night without moving on, and by the grey of the second morning he had at least ruled out exhaustion — what remains is harder and he knows it.

hesta-vorn.name: Hesta Vorn
hesta-vorn.role: Cairn-keeper and mother — the still point a long road runs back to
hesta-vorn.voiceHints: Speaks in full sentences and means them. Unhurried. When Silas appears after a long absence she says his whole name — first, middle, and family-name — not in anger but as if she is counting him back into the world, making sure all of him arrived. Her questions come one at a time and she waits for the answer before asking the next. Her silences are not empty; she is listening to something slightly past what you said.
knowledge: Every stone in her cairn-line and what each one was laid for — some go back three generations, some she placed herself last autumn
The Crossing's seasonal patterns: which roads flood first in the thaw, which traders come through and what they carry, who has not come through this year who should have
How to read a person who has been on the road too long — the particular hollowness behind the eyes, the way they hold their pack strap even after they've set it down
Early-spring flatbread — the precise moment to pull it from the hearthstone so the underside is charred just enough, the way her mother taught and her mother before that
hesta-vorn.wants: For the people she loves to be whole — not triumphant, not even safe, but whole. She'll settle for fed and warm as a start.
hesta-vorn.fears: That one season Silas will not come back down the road, and she will add a stone to the cairn-line and not know what name to lay it for.

reactsToReputation.traveller: puts bread on without being asked
reactsToReputation.in_silas_debt: measured gratitude, not effusive — she'll remember it
reactsToReputation.dangerous: does not flinch, does not welcome; the door is open, the warmth is conditional
reactsToReputation.lost: seats them near the hearth and asks about the road before she asks about them

hesta-vorn.appearance: A woman somewhere in her middle fifties, broad through the shoulders, with Silas's same dark brow and the steadier version of his restlessness settled into competence. Her hair is iron-grey, braided close to the head and pinned with a flat cairn-stone worked smooth — a habit, not an ornament. Flour on her left wrist when she turns. Her hands are large and capable and she does not hide them. She stands in the doorway the way someone stands who has stood in many doorways watching many roads.

abilities.name: Hearthfast
abilities.description: A place Hesta keeps is genuinely harder to come undone in. Those who rest under her roof overnight recover from fatigue and minor wounds as if they had slept a full season's night regardless of the actual hours. The effect is not magic so much as the accumulated intention of every careful thing she has done in that space.
abilities.domainExpression: cairn-warden domestic — the Crossing's principle that a centre held carefully radiates outward

abilities.name: The Full Name
abilities.description: When Hesta speaks someone's full name in full she does something that cannot be faked: she sees them as they are rather than as they have presented themselves on the road. The named person feels it — a moment of being entirely known. Those carrying concealment or deception find it briefly harder to sustain. Those who are genuinely lost find it briefly easier to remember who they were before the road took them.
abilities.domainExpression: cairn-warden naming-rite — the Crossing's function as the place where paths converge and things are called by their right names

abilities.name: Cairn-Tending
abilities.description: Hesta maintains a line of cairns along the approach to her house. Each stone was laid with intention — for a safe return, for a death acknowledged, for a season survived. The line collectively wards the approach: she knows when someone passes it, and she knows something of what they are carrying — not their secrets, but their weight.
abilities.domainExpression: cairn-warden threshold-craft — stone-memory as the Crossing's record of who has passed and what they bore

hesta-vorn.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Kind and domain are independent: a people tends toward positions, an individual holds their own. Her numinous tertiary is not studied — it accreted, the way cairn-stones do, one careful act at a time.

provenance.hint: Silas's mother — a woman who keeps a cairn-line house in Cairnhold, maintains it carefully, bakes flatbread, says her so
provenance.why: She has just turned and spoken — she needs a real name, a full person, to sustain the scene that's beginning

warden-coll.name: Warden Coll
warden-coll.role: Hub Council Member — water and infrastructure portfolio; the official who can act when acting is still possible
warden-coll.voiceHints: Economical to the point of curtness — the man does not perform busyness, he is actually busy. Asks what you want before you have finished sitting down. Speaks in quantities and timelines: not 'the pipe is failing' but 'we lose forty percent flow by midsummer if the east culvert goes unpatched.' Warms slightly, not visibly, when the problem brought to him is real. Has no patience for preamble but considerable patience for a hard fact stated plainly. Will not be flattered. Will not be alarmed before he has the numbers. If Ossian sent you, he will not say it means anything — but he will read the calling-slip before he says anything else.
knowledge: The full infrastructure map of the Hub's water system — not the public version, the one with the problem sections annotated in his own hand
Which repairs have been deferred for how many seasons and why, and what that deferral has cost in compounding risk
The political geometry of the Council well enough to know which votes he can call and which he cannot, and how to move without losing the ones he needs
Ossian's professional judgment well enough that her calling-slip carries weight he would not give a personal introduction
Early-spring thaw load — how much stress the melt season puts on aging infrastructure and exactly how little time there is before the window for intervention closes
warden-coll.wants: To hold the system together long enough that the next Warden inherits something workable. Not glory. Not gratitude. A functioning culvert network and a reserve fund that isn't a fiction.
warden-coll.fears: That the Council will deliberate past the point where deliberation can fix anything — and that when the failure comes, it will be the people at the lowest pipes who drown first.

reactsToReputation.competent: grants more time and more candor than he grants anyone
reactsToReputation.time-waster: ends the meeting without ending it — keeps working while you talk until you understand you are done
reactsToReputation.political: becomes formally polite and shares nothing of consequence
reactsToReputation.referred_by_ossian: reads first, judges after — she has not sent him noise before

warden-coll.appearance: A broad-shouldered man in his late fifties, gone thick through the middle the way engineers do — not soft, just load-bearing. Hair cut close, iron-grey, the same way it has been cut for twenty years. Ink on the heel of his left hand from a map he was tracing when you knocked. Heavy wool coat hung on the back of the door; he works in shirtsleeves even in early spring because the brick hall holds the cold and he does not notice anymore. A north-facing room: the light is flat and good for reading documents. His desk is covered in papers arranged in a system that looks like chaos and is not. He looks up from them at Silas with the expression of a man calculating whether this interruption will cost him ten minutes or an afternoon.
warden-coll.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Coll reasons by load and consequence — syllogist in practice, figurist in how he maps systems, somatic in the residual physical instinct of a man who spent his first decade in the field before he moved behind a desk. Kind and domain are independent: a people tends toward positions, an individual holds their own.
warden-coll.functionsNote: reveal — holds the true state of the infrastructure that public records obscure; bind — the authority to commit Council resources when he chooses to use it; move — the political leverage to unblock action that lower officials cannot. Scene need: the player requires someone who can convert information into institutional motion. Coll is that conversion point.

provenance.hint: Warden Coll — a Hub Council Member who handles water and infrastructure decisions, third floor, north-facing room, brick
provenance.why: Ossian named him as the Council Member who can act on the water crisis — Silas is about to walk into his office with her

offscreen.note: An audit of the eastern culvert ledgers turned up a two-year-old discrepancy that someone before Coll papered over — the reserve fund is smaller than recorded, and now Coll knows it.

warden-coll.history: Coll came to the infrastructure portfolio the way most people come to unglamorous work: nobody else wanted it badly enough to fight him for it. He had spent eleven years before his Council seat in the field survey corps, walking pipe routes in mud-season, taking depth readings in culverts that hadn't been inspected since before he was born. He wrote the annotated map himself over the course of…
warden-coll.relationships: Ossian is the only professional referral he treats as a direct extension of his own judgment. He has met enough surveyors and engineers to know which ones write reports that confirm what the client wants to hear and which ones will put an uncomfortable finding in plain language and stand behind it. Ossian is the latter. When her calling-slip comes through his office he reads it the same day…

veth-coldarrow.name: Veth Coldarrow
veth-coldarrow.role: Jewelry smith of the waygate crescent — reads material before she reads people, quotes price and truth in the same breath
veth-coldarrow.voiceHints: Short sentences. No pleasantries, no flourish — she will name what a piece is before you finish describing what you want. Correct without being unkind. If she says 'it's ready,' it is ready. If she says 'that's wrong for them,' she has already seen it in the metal and will not argue further, only wait for you to agree.
knowledge: The grain and flex of every alloy sold in the waygate valley — can estimate provenance by weight alone
Silas's commission: a paired wedding set, silver-and-copper braid, one wider band and one narrow, sized and finished, wrapped in oiled cloth under the bench — ready two days hence as agreed
Which waygate merchants salt their metal weight and which do not
Early-spring thaw cracks the solder on pieces set in autumn — she warns every customer once, unprompted
veth-coldarrow.wants: Work that holds. To be handed a problem in material, not in sentiment.
veth-coldarrow.fears: A piece leaving her bench wrong and her not catching it — not because of reputation, but because wrong is wrong.

reactsToReputation.honest: does business immediately, no inspection required
reactsToReputation.vague_or_ceremonial: waits them out in silence until they say the plain thing
reactsToReputation.a_collector_or_craftsperson: asks one technical question — genuine, not a test

veth-coldarrow.appearance: A stocky woman in her mid-forties, olive-dark from outdoor working, with short-cropped iron-grey hair held back by a strip of leather. Burn-scars patterned across both hands and the inside of her left wrist like pale lichen. Her apron is dark green oilcloth, same weight as the awning above her — practical, not matched by choice. Eyes the colour of old bronze. She looks at what you are wearing before she looks at your face, and at the metal before either.

activeCommission.description: Paired wedding bands — silver-and-copper braid, one wider, one narrow — sized, finished, wrapped in oiled cloth
activeCommission.readyFor: collection in two days, as agreed
activeCommission.notes: Veth will not release them early. She told Silas a date and that is the date.

veth-coldarrow.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Figurist primary: her work is precise formal making — shape, proportion, material truth. Somatic secondary: the craft lives entirely in the hands and in direct physical reading of the world. Syllogist tertiary: she reasons by rule and consequence, not intuition — if the alloy does X under heat, she has already thought to the end of that chain. Kind and domain are independent.

provenance.hint: a precise jewelry smith at the waygate marketplace crescent — works under a dark-green oilcloth awning, reads material b
provenance.why: Silas commissioned a paired wedding set from her and she will need to persist for the collection scene in two days

edvar-crane.name: Edvar Crane
edvar-crane.role: Mill resident and self-taught water-reader — the man who already knew, and has been waiting for someone to finally ask
edvar-crane.voiceHints: Speaks in the unhurried cadence of a man who has thought something through alone for a long time and is relieved to say it aloud at last. Precise without being academic — the precision of a craftsman who learned by watching things go wrong. He will not exaggerate. He will also not soften. If he pauses, let him; he is choosing the right word, not stalling. Occasional dry wryness, never cruel. The faint bitterness of someone who tried to warn people quietly and was not heard.
knowledge: The exact date the water changed — not roughly, exactly; he wrote it on the door-frame inside the mill
What boiling and settling with wood-ash does to the worst of it, and what it does not fix
That the discolouration runs heavier from the upper fork than the lower, which tells him something is wrong above the second weir
Two other mill families who are quietly doing what he does, and three more who are not and who look grey-tired in a way that worries him
Where the old Waymarker survey stones are set along the upper channel — he walks that ground every early spring to check the snowmelt rate
edvar-crane.wants: Acknowledgment that the crisis is real, upstream, and getting worse — and someone with authority or reach to act on it before people start dying quietly and it gets called a bad season.
edvar-crane.fears: That he will be right about all of it and it will make no difference. That the people who did not listen in autumn will not listen now until the evidence is someone's child.

secondThreadRole.note: Crane is the primary reveal-node for the Second Thread. He does not have answers — he has observations precise enough to point toward answers. His cooperation unlocks the upper-fork investigation and the names of the other affected families. He has been waiting to be believed, not to be told what he already knows.

reactsToReputation.trusted_by_valley: opens immediately, brings out the door-frame record, names every family he knows
reactsToReputation.outsider_unknown: measured — tests with one true thing before offering another
reactsToReputation.dismissive_of_concerns: closes, politely, completely; will answer questions but volunteers nothing
reactsToReputation.already_treating_water: recognises a peer; drops the last of his guardedness and speaks as one careful person to another

edvar-crane.appearance: A heavyset man of around fifty, gone broad across the shoulders from decades at the mill, with hands that are always faintly stained from the wheel-grease he cannot fully wash out. Close-cropped grey hair, a week's worth of beard he doesn't bother with. His face is weathered and watchful — not unfriendly, but accustomed to people not quite looking back. He keeps a tin cup on a hook by his door and never drinks without checking the bottom first. Early spring has him in a heavy canvas coat, unlaced at the collar, with a notebook tucked in the chest pocket.
edvar-crane.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Crane practises no formal tradition — he is a miller who taught himself to read pattern, record time, and reason from evidence. Figurist primary reflects his intuitive map-reading and spatial memory of the watershed; hourkeeper secondary reflects his obsessive log-keeping and change-tracking; syllogist tertiary reflects the quiet deductive chain he has been building alone. Kind and domain are independent.

provenance.hint: Edvar Crane — a mill resident of around fifty, connected to the Waymarker's second thread and the water crisis, already
provenance.why: Crane opened the door — he is the direct subject of the Second Thread quest and needs a stable, fully authored identity

offscreen.note: Crane found a ledger-keeper at the district waypost willing to countersign his water-quality records, giving his claims a second name behind them — still no one with real authority, but the paper trail is thicker now.

edvar-crane.history: Edvar Crane was born in the mill — not metaphorically; his mother went into labour during the spring flood of a year the valley still measures other years against, and his father did not stop working the sluice gate until it was done. He grew up understanding water as a system before he had words for systems: that what comes down the upper fork is not the same as what comes down the lower, that…
edvar-crane.relationships: His nearest relationship is with Pell Sorche, whose family runs the second mill downstream — they do not talk often, but when Edvar shows up at her door before the morning work, she puts the kettle on and does not ask why, because she already knows it is about the water. The other two families who treat and settle as he does are the Anvers household and old Maret who has no family name anyone…

old-shepherd-woman.name: Gweth Callow, the Shepherd of the South March
old-shepherd-woman.role: Old shepherd woman who works the March Road flocks and reads travelers, weather, and valley news with equal accuracy
old-shepherd-woman.voiceHints: Late sixties, unhurried, measures words the way she measures a ewe's gait — one look, then a verdict. Speaks in plain declaratives with no apology for certainty. Uses 'now then' as a full stop. Will name the weather before you think to ask. Does not call people child; calls everyone by their trade or their face — 'you with the road boots' or 'the healer's boy.'
knowledge: Every traveler who has walked the March Road south of Millbrook in the past three seasons — direction, load, company, and whether they came back
The valley's news before it reaches the village: she speaks to drovers, tinkers, and the children sent to fetch strays
Early-spring cloud formations over Callow Ridge that predict late frost with roughly two days' lead — she has been wrong twice in twenty years and remembers both times
Which families in Millbrook are short on winter-feed and which have quietly been selling surplus south — and what that gap means for late lambing
A traveler came through six days ago going south fast, carrying something wrapped in oilcloth, asking no questions and answering none — she noted his boots were valley-made but his hands were not
old-shepherd-woman.wants: The lambing to finish clean, the late frost to hold off three more weeks, and for whatever is moving south along the March Road to do so without dragging trouble back up it.
old-shepherd-woman.fears: That the valley's quiet is the kind that follows something being quietly removed — and that by the time anyone notices the shape of the absence, the lambs will be on the ground and no one will have time to look.

reactsToReputation.honest-traveler: offers the road news freely, may share the fire if she has one going
reactsToReputation.known-liar: gives nothing but weather, and the weather she gives is accurate enough to be useless for evasion
reactsToReputation.healer or midwife: warm, specific, mentions two difficult births in outlying steadings she has been watching with concern

old-shepherd-woman.appearance: A tall woman gone bony with age, weathered to the same grey-brown as the March Road itself. White hair cropped close under a wide felt hat. Staff cut from hedgerow hawthorn, worn smooth at the grip. Boots resoled so many times the layers are visible at the heel. A dog — large, pale, moves like water around the flock — that she addresses by name and in full sentences.
old-shepherd-woman.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Rootkin primary: her knowledge is somatic and seasonal, grown from decades of place. Verist secondary: she names what is true without softening. Horizon tertiary: she reads movement and distance as language — who goes south, who does not return.

provenance.hint: an old shepherd woman on the March Road south of Millbrook — reads travelers fast, names weather accurately, already kno
provenance.why: She appeared in the road encounter and spoke named dialogue; she needs a stable identity so she can recur

offscreen.note: The late frost did not hold — a hard night three days ago caught two dozen newborns before Gweth could move them under shelter, and she lost seven lambs, leaving her shorthanded and grim-tempered going into the remaining weeks of lambing.

old-shepherd-woman.description: Gweth Callow, the Shepherd of the South March

doss-calver-the-fork-keeper.name: Doss Calver, the Fork Keeper
doss-calver-the-fork-keeper.role: Waystation keeper at the March road fork; monitors water conditions along the lower March and serves as a message relay between Mara Wells and travelers on the road
doss-calver-the-fork-keeper.voiceHints: Mid-forties, unhurried to the point of seeming slow — she is not slow. Speaks in plain declarative sentences, often about conditions: the road, the water, the weather. Offers food or water before she offers information. Remembers every person who has passed the fork in the last decade and can tell you what they were carrying.
knowledge: The fork's traffic patterns across every season — who travels when, what loads, what purposes
Water levels and clarity in the lower March channels by direct daily observation; keeps a hand-ruled ledger going back eleven years
Received Silas's delivery; knows exactly what was in it, when it arrived, and what she passed on to Mara Wells
Which messages Mara Wells trusts her to hold and which she sends on immediately, and why the difference matters
The early-spring snowmelt is running faster than her ledger's average; she has noted it and is waiting to see if the pattern holds before saying anything
doss-calver-the-fork-keeper.wants: The road and the water to stay predictable. Failing that, to know as soon as something changes so she can act before it becomes a problem.
doss-calver-the-fork-keeper.fears: A message arriving that she cannot route — one that needs a judgment she does not have the knowledge to make. Also: the day her ledger and the water stop agreeing with each other.

reactsToReputation.reliable: immediate ease, shares her ledger observations without being asked
reactsToReputation.careless: polite, feeds you, tells you nothing that matters

doss-calver-the-fork-keeper.appearance: Broad-faced and broad-shouldered, with the settled look of someone who has stood in the same place through a great deal of weather. Mid-forties, dark hair cut practical and short, skin weathered and winter-pale with the first flush of spring sun starting on the cheekbones. Wears a heavy apron over layered wool. Hands large and ink-stained at the right forefinger from the ledger. The waystation behind her is tidy in the particular way of someone who relies on knowing exactly where everything is.
doss-calver-the-fork-keeper.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Mason primary reflects her ordering, record-keeping, and infrastructural stewardship of the fork. Rootkin secondary reflects her sustained attention to living water conditions and seasonal change. Verist tertiary reflects her plain-spoken commitment to what the evidence actually shows. Kind and domain are independent: a people tends toward positions, an individual holds their own.

provenance.hint: The waystation keeper at the March road fork — a broad-faced woman, practical and unhurried, who monitors water conditio
provenance.why: She received Silas's delivery and will be a recurring relay point on this road; needs a stable identity

a-blazeborn-traveler-in-his-mid-thirties.name: A Blazeborn traveler in his mid-thirties, broad-chested, bur
a-blazeborn-traveler-in-his-mid-thirties.role: someone of Disputed Zone — Left Branch Entrance
a-blazeborn-traveler-in-his-mid-thirties.fears: being undone by the very grain of this place
a-blazeborn-traveler-in-his-mid-thirties.wants: to go on as they are, in a world that won't quite let them

provenance.hint: A Blazeborn traveler in his mid-thirties, broad-chested, burnt-orange coat, a copper-flame fire in a clay bowl — seated
provenance.why: He spoke Silas's parentage on first sight and needs a stable identity and name to recur.

bryn-callowell.name: Bryn Callowell
bryn-callowell.role: Former south-circuit post rider turned deliberate messenger — the man who rode the Zone's margins long enough to know what the margins remember, now waiting at the Left Branch Entrance to deliver something he has been carrying since Silas's father stopped being able to carry it himself
bryn-callowell.voiceHints: Unhurried in all things — speaks the way a man moves who has spent years in a saddle reading weather. Does not front-load. Lets silence do work. When he finally lands a sentence it is already done being revised. He does not apologise for the three days he waited; it is simply what the thing required. Carries gravity without weight — nothing performed about the stillness, it is just how he is arranged.
knowledge: The south circuit's waypoints, seasonal shortcuts, and which crossings are disputed on paper but stable in practice
Edric Vael's work along the zone margin — what it actually was, not the version that got simplified in the retelling
Which parcels Edric never logged and why, and what one of them contained
The Left Branch valley in early spring: where the mud sets overnight, which stone shelf is dry, where to tie a horse so she doesn't founder in the cold
bryn-callowell.wants: To put what he is carrying into Silas's hands and be released from it — not because it is a burden he resents, but because it was always meant to reach the son and it has not yet.
bryn-callowell.fears: That Silas will not be ready to hold the weight of what his father actually was — and that Bryn will misjudge the moment and hand it over anyway, because the alternative is carrying it until he dies.

reactsToReputation.silas: recognition without performance — he simply says 'I know. Sit down.'
reactsToReputation.hostile: does not flinch or escalate; goes very still and waits for the posture to exhaust itself
reactsToReputation.curious: answers the question behind the question, not the question asked

bryn-callowell.appearance: A broad-chested man in his mid-thirties, built for endurance rather than force — the kind of frame that still looks like it could cover forty miles and then split wood. Amber eyes, unhurried. Tawny skin weathered at the neck and the back of the hands from years of open-road riding. His hair is dark, kept short and practical, with the first grey coming in at the temples. He is sitting on a low stone at the valley entrance when Silas arrives — not pacing, not anxious, not asleep. Just waiting, the way a man waits who decided three days ago that this was the correct place to be and has not reconsidered.
bryn-callowell.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Kind and domain are independent: a people tends toward positions, an individual holds their own. Wayfarer primary: Bryn reads the Zone's contested terrain the way a wayfarer reads the land — disputed boundaries, seasonal passage, who controls which crossing and when. Syllogist secondary: years of post-riding required holding contradictory claims simultaneously and routing through them without choosing a side prematurely. Umbral tertiary: the south circuit runs through margins where things are not fully one thing or another; Bryn has learned to move in that half-light without needing to resolve it.

history.southCircuit: Rode the Zone's south circuit for eleven years — a route that skirts both claimed and unclaimed ground, serving settlements that cannot afford to declare alignment. The work required discretion above speed.
history.edricVael: Crossed paths with Silas's father regularly over a six-year stretch. Edric used the post route for things that were not quite post. Bryn never asked. He understood the shape of the work without needing the details, and Edric trusted that understanding.
history.threeYearsAgo: Edric gave Bryn something to hold. Not urgently — quietly, the way a man makes arrangements he hopes will not be needed soon. Said: give it to the boy when he comes south.
history.waiting: Bryn retired from the circuit eighteen months ago. When word reached him that Silas was moving toward the Zone's Left Branch, he rode here and sat down.

bryn-callowell.functionsNote: reveal: Bryn carries knowledge of Edric Vael's actual work — its true shape, its undisclosed pieces — and will surface this to Silas at the right moment. bind: his long witness of Edric's life and his deliberate choice to wait for the son creates a link between Silas's present and his father's past that neither time nor death dissolved.

provenance.hint: Bryn Callowell — a broad-chested Blazeborn man in his mid-thirties, former Zone south-circuit post rider, amber eyes, un
provenance.why: Named himself this beat; needs a stable persistent identity with history tied to Silas's father and the Zone's south cir

tiv-calser.name: Tiv Calser
tiv-calser.role: Hub registry runner — timed courier on a sealed errand she is not supposed to explain
tiv-calser.voiceHints: Brisk and practical, answers in the fewest words the situation allows. Not rude — just running on a clock she can hear ticking. When pressed she doesn't panic; she calculates. Lies by omission rather than invention: 'routine transit' is technically true. Genuinely dislikes being touched or searched. Voice goes flat and careful when she feels the conversation going sideways.
knowledge: The Left Branch Entrance by pre-dawn light — which stones are slick, where the path-markers were moved last season, the sentry rotation she was told to expect and the one she has actually observed
Hub registry seal-protocols: she knows what she is carrying is sealed, who it is addressed to, and that she is not to break the seal under any circumstances short of her own death
The Zone fringe at dawn is the window — later in the morning the disputed stretches get watched more carefully, and she knows why without knowing all of it
How to read a checkpoint stop: whether the party blocking her is authorized, curious, or dangerous, and which of those this is
tiv-calser.wants: To complete the run, log the delivery, and be back inside Hub boundaries before the morning cold burns off the valley. She has another errand this afternoon.
tiv-calser.fears: That the seal gets broken before it reaches the addressee — not because she knows what is inside but because a broken seal means a failed run and a failed run means she loses the routes she has spent two years earning. Also: that whoever has stopped her knows more about the tube's contents than she does.

reactsToReputation.hub_affiliated: cautious professionalism — she will confirm her authorization and expect them to confirm theirs
reactsToReputation.zone_local: polite and minimal; she is not here to make friction with valley people
reactsToReputation.authority: cooperative up to the line where cooperation would require surrendering the tube or breaking the seal; past that line she goes very still
reactsToReputation.threatening: does not run immediately — calculates odds first, then decides; she is faster than she looks

tiv-calser.appearance: A girl of about seventeen, lean and unhurried-looking despite the pace she keeps. Early-spring mud has dried in a hem-stripe on her grey courier trousers. Ash-brown hair cut close on the sides and tied back in a tight knot that will not catch on anything. A runner's satchel worn diagonally, the message-tube slotted inside its own padded sleeve and closed with a brass catch she fingers without thinking whenever she pauses. Pale from a winter of indoor work with the Registry, but her eyes are already adapted to the low valley light. Small scar on her left jaw — old, not recent. She smells of cold air and wax seal.

equipment.carried: Sealed Hub message-tube (brass fittings, wax seal intact, addressee-marked in registry cipher); runner's satchel; a short transit-pass bearing the Hub registrar's stamp; a folding knife she will not lead with
equipment.worn: Grey courier livery, unadorned; fingerless gloves; boots resoled no more than a month ago

currentStatus.errand: Sealed delivery, origin Hub Registry, destination not disclosed to intercepting parties
currentStatus.timing: On schedule at intercept; has a delivery window she has not yet missed but is aware of
currentStatus.mood: Alert, mildly annoyed, not frightened yet

tiv-calser.functionsNote: move — she is the vector; her function is to carry something across a contested threshold. conceal — she will not confirm contents, destination, or sender beyond what her transit-pass legally requires. reveal — if trust is established or the situation forces it, she becomes a thread that leads somewhere: the tube, the sender, the route, the timing of this particular dawn crossing.
tiv-calser.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). She reads situations like problems and solves them on her feet (syllogist primary); the work is physical and her body is her tool (somatic secondary); navigating the Zone fringe at first light, routing through shadow-windows and unmarked crossings, has given her an instinct for what is hidden and where the edges are (umbral tertiary). Kind and domain are independent: a people tends toward positions, an individual holds their own.

provenance.hint: A young Hub registry runner, female, carrying a sealed message-tube through the Zone fringe at dawn — on a timed errand,
provenance.why: She entered the scene with a specific purpose and a sealed Hub message; she needs a stable identity if intercepted

deni-cors.name: Deni Cors
deni-cors.role: Hub-registered pack-runner, south circuit — stopped at the Left Branch entrance with a sealed message for the warden post
deni-cors.voiceHints: Practical and spare — she gives you what you need to know and stops there. Not unfriendly, just calibrated for efficiency; warmth comes out sideways, in small dry observations rather than openings. She is young enough to still find the Disputed Zone a little electric and old enough not to say so. When she names herself she does it plainly, no flourish: 'Deni Cors. South circuit, Hub registered. I'm carrying.' She will not surrender the sealed message to anyone who cannot prove they are warden-post, and she will wait you out on that point without visible anxiety.
knowledge: Every reliable waymark and crossing-point on the south circuit from Hub out to the Left Branch valley mouth — in mud-season and in frost, which are different routes
Which warden posts are reliably staffed, which are not, and which have changed hands enough times that she files a note with Hub after each run
The valley's early-spring moods: where the meltwater crosses the path, where the ground still holds, where it will not
Hub registration protocol — seals, countersigns, chain-of-custody — well enough to spot a forgery and to refuse a handoff that doesn't satisfy the form
deni-cors.wants: To make the hand-off clean, log her arrival, and be back on the south circuit before the afternoon cloud comes in off the ridge.
deni-cors.fears: That the warden post is empty or compromised again — because then she has to decide what to do with a sealed message she is not supposed to open, in a valley that does not fully belong to anyone.

reactsToReputation.warden_affiliated: produces the message immediately, requests a countersign, and relaxes by one visible degree
reactsToReputation.runner_peer: brief solidarity — swaps a single piece of route intelligence, expects one back
reactsToReputation.authority_without_jurisdiction: polite, immovable; she has heard every version of 'I'll take it from here'
reactsToReputation.threatening: she does not run; she goes very still and very quiet and measures the gap to the tree line

deni-cors.appearance: A young woman in her early twenties, lean and weathered past her age from the south circuit's exposure, with the particular muscle of someone who climbs as much as she runs. Skin brown-ruddy from wind and early-spring cold, dark hair pulled back with a cord, one loose strand she has stopped bothering with. Hub registration badge stitched to the left breast of a worn oilcloth coat — the coat has been re-waxed so many times the seams are stiff. Pack riding high and close, properly fitted. The sealed message is not visible; it is inside the coat, not in the pack. She is standing at the valley entrance rather than moving, which means she stopped deliberately — and she is watching the path ahead with the attention of someone who already noticed something before you arrived.

inventory.runner_kit: route-marked oilskin, two-day rations, meltwater flask, short knife (tool not weapon), Hub log-book for delivery signatures

deni-cors.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Kind and domain are independent: a people tends toward positions, an individual holds their own. Wayfarer primary — the south circuit is her lived tradition; somatic secondary — running is a bodily discipline she has refined; syllogist tertiary — Hub registration protocol runs on precise procedure and she has absorbed it.
deni-cors.functionsNote: move: she carries information across contested ground; bind: chain-of-custody protocol — she holds the message to the correct recipient and will not release it outside that constraint; reveal: once the hand-off is satisfied, she may surface route intelligence the party does not have.
deni-cors.recurringCharacterNote: Deni Cors has named herself at this entrance and is now a stable recurring figure on the south circuit. She may be encountered again at any Hub-affiliated post between the valley mouth and the southern waystation chain. Her knowledge of the circuit updates between appearances.

provenance.hint: Deni Cors — Hub registered runner, south circuit, young woman, pack-runner with a sealed message addressed to the Left B
provenance.why: She has stopped and named herself; she is now a recurring character with a stable identity, not a passing figure

offscreen.note: The hand-off she came to make hit a snag: the receiving party wasn't at the agreed point, and she waited past the afternoon cloud window, meaning she missed her south-circuit departure and is now a day behind with no clean explanation logged.

deni-cors.history: Deni Cors has been running the south circuit out of Hub for going on six years — long enough that she did her first mud-season crossing before the current waymark posts were driven in, navigating by the older blaze-cuts on the beech trunks that half the new runners don't know to look for. She came to the work sideways: she'd been a seasonal count-taker for a land assessor who went under, and the…

relationships.Hub senior registrar: The person who told her about the flagged file. She doesn't consider this a debt exactly, but she is more honest with Hub's senior staff than runners are usually required to be — she files detailed notes on warden-post irregularities where others would write 'post unstaffed, message returned.' The registrar reads those notes. Deni knows this because the questions she gets asked on return runs are specific.
relationships.The Left Branch valley mouth, as a place: Not a person, but Deni has a runner's relationship with locations that functions like one. She does not trust the Left Branch entrance the way she trusts the mid-circuit crossings. It is a threshold that has been unreliable enough times that she arrives there already calculating her fallback — who holds the message, where she overnights if she can't hand off, what she tells Hub. She would not say she dislikes running it. She would say it keeps her sharp in a way the easier legs don't.
relationships.Other south-circuit runners: Known by name and by habit. She knows who double-checks their seals and who doesn't, who files honest post-condition notes and who smooths them over. She doesn't socialize much on layovers but she talks shop freely, and other runners on the circuit tend to come to her when something feels off about a run they've been given. She usually has a prior note on the post in question.

voss-of-the-chalk-and-counter.name: Voss of the Chalk and Counter
voss-of-the-chalk-and-counter.role: Food-stall keeper at the Crossing — feeds half the market and forgets nothing she is owed
voss-of-the-chalk-and-counter.voiceHints: Unhurried and firm — the voice of someone who has already heard every excuse and found them all wanting, but will let you finish anyway. She does not raise her voice to make a point; she lowers it. When she quotes your tab back at you, she quotes the date, the dish, the weather that day, and what you said when you left. She does not embellish. She does not need to.
knowledge: Every unpaid tab in the Crossing, carried in a chalk-ledger she updates each dusk and recites from memory by dawn
Which stalls cut their weights, which water their broth, and which trade in last-season goods relabelled as new — she neither gossips nor protects them, but she knows
The rhythms of the Crossing better than anyone: who comes when, who avoids whose eye, which rows heat up before they boil over
That Silas owes her one bowl of root-and-barley stew, two flatbreads, and a cup of pressed-fruit from the last of autumn — she can name the day without checking the ledger
voss-of-the-chalk-and-counter.wants: To be paid what she is owed, not because she needs the coin, but because a debt unpaid is a small untruth left standing in the world — and she keeps a clean stall.
voss-of-the-chalk-and-counter.fears: That the Crossing will soften into a place where debts dissolve in goodwill and no one trusts a price anymore; that fair dealing will be eaten alive by charm.

reactsToReputation.honest: serves them first, no waiting, best cut of whatever is warm
reactsToReputation.charming_debtor: pleasant, immovable — she will smile and recite the ledger entry in the same breath
reactsToReputation.reliable_payer: small extra portion, no comment made, none needed
reactsToReputation.troublemaker: watches without watching; has alerted the row before before and will again

voss-of-the-chalk-and-counter.appearance: A broad-shouldered woman in her mid-fifties, dark-complexioned, her grey-streaked hair pinned back under a linen wrap dyed the colour of old mustard. Trader's apron — heavy canvas, patched at the pocket where the chalk lives — over a well-worn wool dress. Hands that have worked hot iron pots so long they no longer feel the heat. She stands behind her counter the way a wall stands: present, not aggressive, simply there. The chalk-ledger hangs on a cord at her hip; she touches it the way another person might touch a knife.
voss-of-the-chalk-and-counter.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Voss is not a practitioner in any formal sense — she practises the figurist's art in the keeping of accounts, the syllogist's logic in the settling of disputes, and carries an almost instinctive sense of social weight that brushes the numinous without ever naming it. Kind and domain are independent: a people tends toward positions, an individual holds their own.

stall.name: Voss's Counter
currentOfferings: root-and-barley broth — thin this time of year but honest
flatbreads from yesterday's grain, still good
pressed dried fruit from the last of winter stores
boiled eggs, six per tray, chalked price visible from four stalls away
stall.ledgerNote: Chalk-ledger holds forty-one names as of this morning. Silas is line nineteen.

silasTension.debt: one bowl root-and-barley, two flatbreads, one pressed-fruit cup — last autumn, third week
silasTension.herPosition: She is not angry. She is waiting. There is a difference, and Silas should understand it.
silasTension.recurringPressure: She will not chase him through the row. She will simply be at her stall every time he passes, and she will say his name, and she will say the amount, and she will say the date. Every time. Pleasantly. Until it is settled.

provenance.hint: A market-stall holder at the Crossing — mid-fifties, trader's apron, chalk-ledger keeper, unhurried but firm; runs a foo
provenance.why: She has caught Silas in the market row over an unpaid meal from last season and needs to be a recurring presence at this

bren-of-the-sheaf-and-bowl.name: Bren of the Sheaf and Bowl
bren-of-the-sheaf-and-bowl.role: Stall-holder at the Crossing market row — patient measurer of grain, pulse, and people
bren-of-the-sheaf-and-bowl.voiceHints: Unhurried. Weighs words the way he weighs grain — no extras, none short. Answers slowly not from dullness but because he genuinely considers. Will repeat a price exactly once; after that he writes it in the ledger and turns it to face you. Has a habit of naming things by what they are used for rather than what they are called.
knowledge: What the Crossing moves in early spring — which goods are scarce, which are flooding in, who is underselling and why
Faces: he has traded here long enough that he knows returning buyers by their first purchase, years back
The ledger — every transaction since he took the stall, cross-indexed by buyer, date, and commodity; he can find any entry in under a minute
Which neighbouring stall-holders are honest, which cut their measures, and which are having a hard season and won't say so
bren-of-the-sheaf-and-bowl.wants: A fair market — not a perfect one, just one where the weights are true and nobody goes home having been cheated without knowing it.
bren-of-the-sheaf-and-bowl.fears: That the ledger will one day show him something he cannot balance: a pattern of small wrongs he enabled by saying nothing.

reactsToReputation.honest: easy credit, a better price on the second visit, remembered by name
reactsToReputation.known_cheat: polite, correct, and will not sell in bulk — he writes the transaction down with extra care
reactsToReputation.newcomer: patient, explains the Crossing's customs without being asked, assumes good faith until shown otherwise

bren-of-the-sheaf-and-bowl.appearance: A broad-shouldered man in his mid-fifties, gone soft at the middle but still strong through the hands. Skin weathered to a warm umber from years at an open stall. Grey at the temples, the rest still dark brown, kept short. A canvas apron with deep pockets — one holds the ledger, one holds a folded cloth for wiping the scale pan. His eyes move to the scale when he is thinking and to your face when he has decided.
props: A brass balance scale, old and well-maintained, kept level on a wooden block he planed flat himself
The ledger — thick, cloth-bound, pages soft with handling; the current year's entries in a small careful hand, older years in a hand that was looser before it learned to be precise
A row of clay jars behind the stall holding spelt, dried peas, millet, lentils, and early-spring barley — the first of the season, which he has priced honestly despite it being short
bren-of-the-sheaf-and-bowl.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Figurist primary: his world is counts, weights, and ledger-columns — the concrete record as truth. Syllogist secondary: he reasons from what the numbers show, draws quiet conclusions about people and seasons. Numinous tertiary: a residual, almost unconscious sense that honest measure is something close to sacred, inherited from whoever taught him the trade. Kind and domain are independent.

provenance.hint: Bren — Sheaf and Bowl stall-holder, Crossing market row, fifties, patient trader who keeps a careful ledger
provenance.why: Named and met this beat; needs a stable record to recur

bren-of-the-sheaf-and-bowl.description: Bren of the Sheaf and Bowl

the-low-lamp-inn.name: The Low Lamp Inn
the-low-lamp-inn.descriptionSeed: Tucked into the lower tier of the Edge District where the light-guide streets run closest to the valley floor, the Low Lamp sits over a junction conduit — the glow rises through pale stone floors and fills the common room from below, warm and directionless as afternoon through cloud. The building is two storeys of dressed sandstone with deep-set windows fitted with diffusion panels so the light inside is never harsh. The beds are thick-mattressed, the bath-room fed by a cistern the owner keeps properly heated, and the linens smell of cedar oil. Maret Doss, who runs it, is a compact woman of sixty-odd years whose conversational range does not include your name, your business, where you've come from, or where you're going. She does ask whether you'd prefer the bath before or after supper, because the water pressure is better before the evening crowd. She has been here since before the last treaty renegotiation and expects to be here after the next. The common room is quiet enough to think in, which is unusual for the Edge District and not accidental.
the-low-lamp-inn.encounterFlavor: A common room lit gold-from-below where two or three guests eat separately and don't introduce themselves; early-spring rain ticking against diffusion panels; the smell of cedar, hot water, and whatever Maret is cooking that isn't your concern unless you'd like a bowl. Occasionally a figure comes in from the cold, exchanges a look with Maret, goes upstairs, and is not there in the morning.
questSeeds: A guest in the corner room has been here eleven nights and hasn't come down today — Maret won't say how she knows something is wrong, only that she'd like it handled quietly and without the District wardens

The light-guide conduit under the inn has been cycling strangely at the third hour of the night, waking guests with a pulse of light brighter than it should be — someone with knowledge of Radiant infrastructure could trace it, if they were careful about who found out they were looking

A sealed letter was left with Maret for a guest who checked in under a name that matches someone Silas or Pell have reason to recognize — Maret will not confirm or deny the guest exists, but she hasn't burned the letter

Maret's cedar oil supplier hasn't come up from the valley floor in three weeks; she mentions this once, flatly, and doesn't mention it again — but the route he travels crosses ground that has been quietly problematic

provenance.hint: a modest but genuinely comfortable inn in the Edge District of the Radiant Plateau — warm, lit from below by the light-g
provenance.why: Silas and Pell need a named, returnable inn in the Edge District to spend the night — it will be a place they may return

what-the-mill-keeps.name: What the Mill Keeps
what-the-mill-keeps.pressure: Grael's fall has reached Millbrook not as rumor but as verified fact — a travelling assessor's writ nailed to the granary door, signed and counter-signed. The valley does not erupt. It exhales. Then, quietly, it begins to count. Every shortfall in the seed-ledger, every bridge timber that rotted faster than it should, every widow who could not make her tithe and lost the eastern field — all of it is suddenly legible. Millbrook is a community that trusts its records, and its records, read correctly now, tell a damning story. The pressure is not vengeance. It is restitution arithmetic, and the numbers do not yet balance.
what-the-mill-keeps.tendency: The valley moves toward orderly repair — petitions filed, parcels measured, debts formally disputed — but the process is generating unexpected friction between those who lost the most and those who administered Grael's arrangements locally, often in good faith. Old trust between neighbors is under quiet audit. The grain of Millbrook is that it will endure and regularize rather than break, but the regularizing is slow and the wounds of small betrayals are precise.
what-the-mill-keeps.ifIgnored: The restitution process grinds through distant administrative channels without local witness or pressure. Durrick Soll's quiet acts of repair go unnamed and unformalized, so no reconciliation actually occurs — just awkwardness that calcifies. Oswen Fartle retires her ledger to a locked chest and says nothing. Maret Hohn gets a partial settlement in two years: coin value, not land. The valley remains peaceful and orderly and is permanently a little smaller than it was, in a way no single person can point to.
what-the-mill-keeps.ifEngaged: If someone convenes the assembly Oswen needs, or extends the named mercy Durrick cannot ask for, or presses the assessor's process on Maret's behalf with local testimony in hand — the valley demonstrates what strong order and strong peace actually accomplish together: a full accounting, a returned field, a neighbor restored to neighbor. Durrick becomes the first to sign the commons-reform covenant Oswen drafts. The Millbrook ledger becomes a model document cited two valleys over when the same pattern is discovered elsewhere. The place does not merely survive Grael's fall — it becomes the proof that the fall was worth making.

the-craft-that-drank-from-still-water.name: The Craft That Drank From Still Water
the-craft-that-drank-from-still-water.pressure: The waking beneath the substrate has changed the feel of the Left Branch Entrance — the valley hums at a frequency its practitioners never trained for. The Lodgekeepers of the Threshold, a loose compact of valley-born shapers who have drawn on the substrate for three generations of small, precise work (sealing passes, quieting rockslip, easing difficult births), are discovering their techniques no longer land true. Wards placed at dawn have inverted by dusk. A sealing that should have held a crumbling retaining wall instead sheared it clean. Two of their number felt something answer when they reached — something that was not the substrate they knew. The compact is fracturing along the only fault line that matters: those who believe they must stop working until they understand what they are now drinking from, and those who believe that stopping is itself the catastrophe, that the valley depends on them and that adapting in motion is the only survival.
the-craft-that-drank-from-still-water.tendency: escalating — the longer the compact delays resolution, the more dependent valley infrastructure quietly fails. The waking does not pause to let practitioners catch up. Each week that passes without a new working model, one more load-bearing piece of the valley's subtle architecture slips. The pressure toward manifestation instability compounds: practitioners attempting old forms on the new substrate are generating the exact chaotic partial-manifestations that feed arc_manifestation_storm, without understanding they are doing so.
crossesRegions: Disputed Zone (border outposts dependent on Lodgekeeper sealing work)
any settlement downstream of the valley's retaining infrastructure
the-craft-that-drank-from-still-water.ifIgnored: The Lodgekeeper compact quietly collapses — not dramatically, but by attrition. Practitioners stop working one by one, citing conscience or fear. The valley's subtle infrastructure degrades over the course of a season. A retaining slope fails in early autumn and takes a stretch of the left branch road with it, cutting one of the Disputed Zone's border outposts from resupply. The partial-manifestations generated by the compact's failed attempts during the fracture period have already seeded three unstable nodes in the valley floor, which feed arc_manifestation_storm without anyone in the valley understanding why strange weather now pools here. Veld Thrace leaves with her notes and no obligation to share them.
the-craft-that-drank-from-still-water.ifEngaged: The players enter a compact that is three days from open fracture and does not know it. Senne's secret is the load-bearing element — getting her to speak, or discovering what she is hiding, determines whether the compact's crisis becomes a controlled break or a shattering. There is a genuine technical problem to solve: the substrate has changed, the old forms are unstable, and someone has to do the first working on the new ground or prove it cannot be done. Veld Thrace's knowledge of theoretical frameworks for substrate-shift is real and useful and costs something. Corryn's map is accurate and needs to reach the right ears at the right moment. Resolution can take several shapes — a reformed compact working cautiously with the new substrate, a legitimate stop-work while the valley learns to carry itself, or a compact that breaks but whose knowledge is preserved rather than lost. Each outcome has different weight on arc_manifestation_storm: a successful new working framework locally damps the instability; a chaotic fracture amplifies it. The waking beneath does not intervene, but Senne's account of it — if she speaks — is the first detailed witness testimony of what the waking is like from the inside of contact, which presses directly on The Second Manifestation.
